dive.says: A fall-through in the equator's plane can go down to the top of the air, 1.13 radii, and come back out free. A clock falling through there loses 106.4 µs a day against one far away. Over the pass its clock falls 24.3 µs behind a far one.

park.says: The closest it can park in the equator's plane is 1.13 radii: inside that the air is deadly. A clock on an orbit there loses 79.8 µs a day against one far away.

references.text: Newtonian gravity for a spherical body, e.g. de Pater, I. and Lissauer, J. J. 2015, Planetary Sciences, 2nd edn, Cambridge University Press, chapter 2.

Roederer, J. G. 1970, Dynamics of Geomagnetically Trapped Radiation, Springer (Physics and Chemistry in Space 2): Liouville's theorem along a field line, so a pitch-angle spread sin^n of the equatorial angle keeps its shape and scales as (B_eq / B)^(n/2).
Walt, M. 1994, Introduction to Geomagnetically Trapped Radiation, Cambridge University Press, chapter 3: the dipole field along a line, B / B_eq = sqrt(1 + 3 sin^2 lat) / cos^6 lat.
Schwarzschild, K. 1916, Über das Gravitationsfeld eines Massenpunktes nach der Einsteinschen Theorie, Sitzungsber. Preuss. Akad. Wiss., 189
Misner, C. W., Thorne, K. S. and Wheeler, J. A. 1973, Gravitation, W. H. Freeman (Schwarzschild geometry, chapters 25 and 31)
